anomalies.observed: D3 is a 12 V zener connected with its cathode (pin 1, K) to GND and its anode (pin 2, A) to the T3 gate net /G_RPP. R7 pulls /G_RPP to T3 source (/+24V_F), so with a 24 V input D3 is forward-biased and clamps the gate to about 0.7 V above ground, giving VGS approximately -23.3 V for the P-channel AON6407.
anomalies.expected: For the high-side P-channel reverse-polarity/load switch, the 12 V zener should be oriented to clamp the gate near +12 V relative to ground (cathode to /G_RPP/gate, anode to GND) or otherwise limit VGS to within the device rating, about -12 V when 24 V is present.

evidence.quote: The PCB includes "reverse polarity protection, TVS diodes, proper isolation"

anomalies.impact: The T3 gate-source voltage can exceed the AON6407 absolute maximum under normal 24 V operation, risking gate-oxide stress/failure and unreliable reverse-polarity protection.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows a reversed zener clamp on the high-side P-channel protection MOSFET T3, which can over-stress its gate-source voltage; other apparent mismatches seem to be documentation/reference numbering issues rather than connectivity faults.
